mappings.note: Her immediate feeling at the Saavan cloud -- expectancy and joy at Hari's coming, which the pad implies. Rejected LO-137: no line states the feeling.
What 'daamin' SYMBOLISES -- the momentary flash that kindles hope of darshan. Cited at goal level because no outcome among the 16 covers poetic symbol; LO-138 is folk song and tale specifically.
Which quality of the wind draws her -- its coolness and pleasantness, named in the pad. Rejected LO-134: the epithets are given.
Which songs Giridharnagar sings (aanand mangal) -- located in the closing line. Rejected LO-138: the item asks what is sung, not about the genre.
The SYMBOLIC weight of the 'kshudra ghantika' at his waist -- keyed as the subtle sound of devotion. Cited at goal level because none of the 16 outcomes covers poetic symbol.
Which sound 'noopur shabd rasaal' conveys -- the phrase turns on 'rasaal', a literary word for sweet or savoury. Rejected LO-137: the diction is the demand.
What her lord's nature is towards saints -- giving joy and shelter, her claim about him. Rejected LO-137: the second half of the answer goes past the line.
By seeing what the heart finds peace -- his beguiling form, which the pad conveys without stating. Rejected LO-137 for that reason.
Which month the second pad concerns (Saavan) -- located. Rejected LO-136: a fact, not the text's use.
By which names she addresses her lord -- Nandlal and Bhakt Vachhal Gopal, both quoted. Rejected LO-140, kept for the items that unpack an epithet.
What the poet's wish is -- that Krishna come to dwell in her eyes. Her idea, stated as a plea. Rejected LO-137: the wish is her position, not a locatable fact.
What 'bhanak suni hari aavan ki' means -- the item turns on 'bhanak', a faint inkling. Rejected LO-134: the word carries it.
What her lord is like -- joy to saints, ever protecting his devotees: her claim. Rejected LO-137: the phrasing generalises past the line.
To whom both pads are dedicated -- placing the two texts as a pair. Rejected LO-138: the item asks the dedicatee, not about the devotional genre.
What she called pleasing to the heart -- the fine drops and the cool wind, both located. Rejected LO-131: named, not rendered.
The bhaavaarth of the 'mohani moorati' line -- restating what Mira conveys of his form. Rejected LO-140: the words are plain; the sense of the whole line is wanted.
Which form of Nandlal the first pad describes -- image, complexion, eyes, flute, garland: a catalogue gathered by close reading. Rejected LO-131: collecting details, not rendering a scene.
Explicate 'kshudra ghantika katitat sobhit, noopur shabd rasaal' -- four archaic words carry the line. Rejected LO-134: the diction is the obstacle.
The effect of Saavan on Mira's heart in the second pad -- her joy at the inkling of his coming. Rejected LO-137: the connection is hers to be read.

What picture of nature the 'daamin dam kai' line paints -- the learner must render the lightning and the unbroken shower in their own words. Rejected LO-137, which fits the item that only names the event.

Which feeling for her lord both pads express -- deep bhakti and prem. A judgement about the devotional register of these sung pads. Rejected LO-134: the item asks about the kind of devotion, not one idea of hers.

Describe Nandlal's beauty in the first poem IN YOUR OWN WORDS -- rendering a described figure. Rejected LO-137 because of that instruction. NOTE: the stored key brings in a peacock crown and makara earrings, which this pad does not contain -- its details are the flute, the vaijayanti garland, the wide eyes, the waist bells and the anklets.
The effect of Saavan on her heart in the second poem -- joy and the sense of his approach. Rejected LO-137: inferred, not stated.
Why she calls him 'bhakt vachhal Gopal' -- her claim that he removes his devotees' sorrows. Rejected LO-140: the reason, not the word's form, is wanted.
The meaning of the 'kshudra ghantika' line -- glossed word by word as the small bells at the waist-band and their sweet sound. Rejected LO-134: the diction is the demand.

Describe the beauty of the Saavan season on the strength of the pad -- the learner renders the scene of clouds, lightning, fine drops and cool wind. Rejected LO-137: the demand is a description, not a fact.
Describe Krishna's beauty and adornment -- again the learner renders a figure in their own words. Rejected LO-137: a description, not retrieval.

The marks of Mira's bhakti -- sagun rather than nirgun, with surrender and love above social propriety. That is an appreciation of the devotional tradition her sung pads belong to. Rejected LO-134: the item characterises a tradition, not one idea.
Describe Nandlal's beauty with his physical marks and ornaments, and bring out her devotion -- a rendering of the figure. Rejected LO-137: the instruction is to describe at length.

Analyse the feelings drawn in the second pad and the relation between nature and her emotion -- reading her design. Rejected LO-131: the demand is analysis of the link, not a description of the scene.
Compare her love and surrender across the two pads and say whether the expression differs -- weighing her ideas against each other. Rejected LO-135: no preference of the learner's is argued.

Evaluate the pads and comment on their LANGUAGE, RAS and ALANKAR -- explicitly the apparatus of poetic appreciation. Cited at goal level because no outcome among the 16 covers ras or alankar; LO-140 concerns the learner's own use of words, not the criticism of a poet's craft.

The central feeling of both pads and their place in Mira's life and the bhakti tradition -- situating them in that tradition. Rejected LO-136: the item asks their significance within a genre, not their usefulness to a reader.
How her love and surrender to her deity are expressed, with examples -- the devotional idiom of the tradition. Rejected LO-134: the item characterises her bhakti rather than one idea.
How nature and feeling are brought together in both poems -- her method of joining the two. Rejected LO-131: the demand is the synthesis, not a description.
Which form of bhakti and prem the pads show (maadhurya bhaav) -- naming a category of the devotional tradition. Rejected LO-134: a genre judgement.
Which month's rain is described (Shraavan) -- located in the printed extract. Rejected LO-134: a fact. This key is the correct one, against the earlier item in this chapter that keys Vaishakh.
When she gets the inkling of his coming -- when the Saavan cloud rains. Rejected LO-134: stated in the extract.
Meaning of 'daamin dam kai' -- the flashing of lightning, glossed from an archaic construction. Rejected LO-137: lexical.
Why Saavan pleases her -- because the raining cloud makes her feel Krishna is coming. Her reasoning. Rejected LO-137: the connection is hers to be read.
